clientsExcluded: CalDAV and CardDAV client apps on phones, tablets, and desktops (for example Apple Calendar, DAVx5, Thunderbird)
Device or vendor cloud backups configured within those client apps

evidence.claim: The MOS package projects only RADICALE_ADMIN_USERNAME, RADICALE_ADMIN_PASSWORD, RADICALE_CALENDAR_DISPLAYNAME, and the owner's optional MOS_SMTP_* email relay values into the radicale service and mounts one local data volume; the mcp service gets only RADICALE_ADMIN_USERNAME, RADICALE_ADMIN_PASSWORD and the generated MOS_AI_KEY, and mounts nothing. Neither sets any analytics, update-check, external-service, or telemetry variable, nor any of the UID, GID, or RADICALE_CONFIG_* variables the image's own entrypoint acts on.

The package entrypoint configures htpasswd authentication with bcrypt against a local /data/users file and creates the bootstrap user, a default calendar collection named from the locally supplied RADICALE_CALENDAR_DISPLAYNAME value, and one locally generated all-day starter event on the local data volume; no upstream account or service is contacted during provisioning, and the starter event contains no identifying data beyond a random UID and the install date.

Radicale 3.9.2 is a self-hosted CalDAV/CardDAV server that serves DAV over its own port and stores collections on the local filesystem; its documentation and its 3.7.7 to 3.9.2 release notes contain no mention of telemetry, usage analytics, update checks, or phone-home behaviour.

The pinned tomsquest/docker-radicale 3.9.2.0 build installs Radicale 3.9.2 on Alpine 3.24.4 and Python 3.14.10. Its Dockerfile differs from 3.9.1.1 only in the default version string, its entrypoint, default config and image user (uid 2999) are byte-identical, and its installed Python packages differ only in Radicale itself; passlib and bcrypt are still installed and requests and pika are still absent. Radicale 3.9.1 to 3.9.2 changes no configuration default and adds no dependency or network code outside its tests: it changes how CS:getctag is computed, skips broken items when listing, bounds open-ended recurrence searches, and fixes LDAP SNI and SSL-protocol handling this package does not use. The build introduces no outbound analytics, licensing, or update service.
evidence.source: tomsquest/docker-radicale diff 3.9.1.1..3.9.2.0, Kozea/Radicale diff v3.9.1..v3.9.2, and pip list plus entrypoint and config checksums in the built 3.9.1.1 and 3.9.2.0 package images

evidence.claim: Radicale supports optional IMAP, LDAP, OAuth2, and SMTP authentication backends that would contact an external server. None are reachable in this package: the entrypoint pins auth type to htpasswd against a local file, and no manifest field exposes an alternative authentication backend.

Radicale 3.8.0 and 3.8.1 add collection sharing by token or map, sharing by group, a [group] backend, and a /.mobileconfig profile; 3.8.2 adds a free/busy view (GET ?view=freebusy, a WebUI link to it, and an 'f' rights permission). Sharing and groups default to off ([sharing] type and [group] type are none), the package entrypoint writes only [auth] and [hook], and the image's default rights are owner_only, so no collection or free/busy view is reachable without the owner's password. /.mobileconfig and the free/busy view are generated on the server for the signed-in user and contact nothing. 3.9.0 adds a property-locking permission and 3.9.1 adds map-based sharing to self, an 'S' rights permission, and a free/busy view that returns one VEVENT per busy period; in 3.9.1 [sharing] type and [group] type still default to none and [rights] type to owner_only, and the image's config sets none of them. 3.9.2 adds no sharing, group or rights feature and leaves those defaults unchanged.
evidence.source: Radicale 3.9.2 radicale/config.py and CHANGELOG.md; the 3.9.2.0 image's /config/config; apps/radicale/entrypoint.sh

evidence.claim: All calendar and contact data is persisted to the single data:/data package volume, so CalDAV/CardDAV collections stay within the MOS runtime rather than any upstream store.

A packet capture on the Docker bridge of the built package container recorded no DNS queries and no packets to any routable address across first boot with user and calendar provisioning, idle time, authenticated and rejected CalDAV requests, an event write, a calendar export, recovery from a hard kill, and a clean restart; the only captured traffic was the test client's requests to the Radicale port plus link-local ARP and IPv6 multicast housekeeping from the kernel.
evidence.source: tcpdump capture of the locally built package image (docker0 bridge), 2026-07-31

evidence.claim: The docker-radicale image maintainer confirmed in writing that to his knowledge the image contains no telemetry, noting that nearly all behaviour comes from Radicale itself.

MOS wires Radicale's [hook] email notifications to the shared, optional MOS email relay. Radicale can email the attendees of a calendar event when it changes; the entrypoint writes this [hook] configuration only when the owner has set a relay under Settings → Email relay, and removes it when they have not, so Radicale sends no mail by default. When set, notices go through the owner's own chosen provider. This is the narrowest of Radicale's outbound features — attendee notices only — and is separate from the authentication backends above; MOS never uses the relay itself. Radicale 3.9.1 adds opt-in iTIP scheduling messages to the email hook; it is off by default (itip_enabled = False), MOS does not set it, and the 3.9.1.1 package logs itip_enabled=False when a relay is configured, so the hook keeps sending only the attendee notices described here. Radicale 3.9.2 changes only logging in the email hook.
evidence.source: apps/radicale/entrypoint.sh, apps/radicale/manifest.json, and the email hook's startup log in the built 3.9.1.1 package image

evidence.claim: The mcp service is the MCP server MOS ships for AI access. It is built from the same pinned docker-radicale image, runs only the package's own mcp-server.py on the Python standard library under the image's radicale user, and its only outbound connection is CalDAV and CardDAV to http://radicale:5232 on the package network. It has no route: the host publishes it on loopback for Suite Manager alone, and it answers only requests carrying the key MOS generated for this install. It signs in as the Radicale user from the install form, and offers listing calendars and events, searching contacts, adding an event and moving or renaming a single event. An event it adds carries no ATTENDEE or ORGANIZER, and it refuses to change an event that has an ATTENDEE, so it never sets off the email hook's attendee notices; it has no tool that deletes anything or changes a contact.

A packet capture inside the network namespace of the built 3.8.3.0 package container, on every interface including loopback, recorded no DNS queries and no packets to any address other than the test client across a start on a data volume written by the 3.8.1.1 package, rejected and authenticated requests, a calendar export, the free/busy view, the web UI, and 30 seconds idle; the only other traffic was the image's own loopback healthcheck and an IPv6 router solicitation from the kernel. Capturing inside the namespace covers lookups to Docker's embedded resolver, which a bridge capture cannot see.
evidence.source: tcpdump capture of the locally built package image, 2026-10-25

evidence.claim: The MOS E2E network capture recorded this package on a MOS lab on 2026-10-05, through install, the package's own journey (signing in, creating a calendar and an address book in the web UI, and putting an event over CalDAV and a contact over CardDAV), a backup and a restore. It recorded every DNS lookup the package's containers made, read inside each container, every connection they opened to a public address, read on the Docker bridges, and every request the browser made to a host outside the suite. A control lookup and connection sent from inside each container showed up, so silence here is a measurement rather than a capture that failed. The container made no lookup and no connection, and the browser made no request outside the suite.
evidence.source: MOS E2E `npm run e2e -- @app-cycle radicale`, run 20261005-112126-app-cycle-radicale (network/report.md), on the package version reviewed before this revision

telemetryControls.claim: Radicale ships no telemetry, analytics, or update-check behaviour, so no telemetry-disabling configuration is required or applied by the package.

openQuestions: The 2026-07-31, 2026-10-06, 2026-10-25, 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-19 packet captures covered minutes of provisioning, active use, and restarts; outbound behaviour on longer timers than that window is excluded by the code and build-definition review rather than by observation. The lab E2E network step, which reads DNS inside the container, last ran on 2026-10-05 against an earlier package version and has not yet run against 3.8.3, 3.9.1 or 3.9.2.
No packet capture has yet covered the mcp service; that its only connection is to the radicale service rests on the review of mcp-server.py, which opens no other address.
CalDAV/CardDAV client apps may copy synced calendar and contact data into device or vendor cloud backups depending on each client's settings, which is outside the server package's control.
The package provisions a single bootstrap Radicale user; multi-user authentication, password rotation, and DAV auto-discovery are future package work not covered by this review.
